info.name: Harbor — Shopping Demo Workflow
info.description:
The shopping demo end to end over MCP 2026-07-28: three services are registered (product, order, tasks); the workflow uses only product and order.

1. Discover the services. 2. Browse products with INR prices and stock. 3. Read one product. 4. Order within the INR 5,000 limit (runs directly). 5–6. Order above the limit: Harbor pauses for approval; answering Yes places the same order. 7–8. Another order above the limit; answering No places nothing. 9. List my orders. 10. Try to delete an order: the gateway policy denies it. 11. The order still exists.

The order service derives the customer from the bearer, so no customer ID is sent. Run with examples/demo/start.sh (gateway on :3333) and run the requests top to bottom; they chain ids through collection variables. CI runs this collection through tests/postman/run-collection.mjs from tests/demo_e2e.py.

item.name: 1. discover_services — product, order and tasks are available

request.description: The gateway exposes three services. Only product and order are relevant to shopping; tasks is unrelated.

exec: let payload; try { payload = JSON.parse(rpc.result.content[0].text) } catch (e) { payload = undefined }
pm.test('product, order and tasks are registered', () => { const names = payload.map(s => s.service); ['product', 'order', 'tasks'].forEach(n => pm.expect(names).to.include(n)); });

request.description: GET /products returns every product with its INR price, stock and availability.

exec: let payload; try { payload = JSON.parse(rpc.result.content[0].text) } catch (e) { payload = undefined }
pm.test('12 products with price and stock', () => { pm.expect(payload).to.have.length(12); payload.forEach(p => { pm.expect(p.price).to.be.a('number'); pm.expect(p.stock).to.be.a('number'); }); });
pm.test('the USB-C Hub is out of stock', () => pm.expect(payload.find(p => p.id === 'p004').inStock).to.eql(false));

item.name: 3. product — read one product before ordering

request.description: GET /products/{id} gives the current price and stock for the order.

exec: let payload; try { payload = JSON.parse(rpc.result.content[0].text) } catch (e) { payload = undefined }
pm.test('water bottle costs INR 899 and is in stock', () => { pm.expect(payload.price).to.eql(899); pm.expect(payload.stock).to.be.above(2); pm.expect(payload.inStock).to.eql(true); });

request.description: An order within INR 5,000 is allowed without approval. No customer ID is sent.

exec: let payload; try { payload = JSON.parse(rpc.result.content[0].text) } catch (e) { payload = undefined }

pm.test('order confirmed for the caller-token-derived demo customer', () => { pm.expect(payload.status).to.eql(201); pm.expect(payload.order.amountInr).to.eql(1798); pm.expect(payload.order.customerId).to.match(/^cust-/); });

request.description: Above INR 5,000 Harbor pauses before the order reaches the backend.

exec: let payload; try { payload = JSON.parse(rpc.result.content[0].text) } catch (e) { payload = undefined }
pm.test('approval message names the order rule', () => pm.expect(rpc.result.inputRequests.approval.params.message).to.include('5000 INR'));

item.name: 6. approval — Yes: the same order is placed

request.description: The human answers Yes (approve: true). Harbor resumes the original program and places the order once.

exec: if (!pm.collectionVariables.get('approveRequestState')) throw new Error('Run step 5 first.');
let payload; try { payload = JSON.parse(rpc.result.content[0].text) } catch (e) { payload = undefined }

pm.test('office chair order created', () => { pm.expect(payload.status).to.eql(201); pm.expect(payload.order.productName).to.eql('Ergonomic Office Chair'); pm.expect(payload.order.amountInr).to.eql(12999); });

request.description: A second high-value order pauses for approval.

exec: let payload; try { payload = JSON.parse(rpc.result.content[0].text) } catch (e) { payload = undefined }
pm.test('approval message names the order rule', () => pm.expect(rpc.result.inputRequests.approval.params.message).to.include('5000 INR'));

request.description: The human answers No (approve: false). The execution is denied and the order is never sent.

exec: if (!pm.collectionVariables.get('rejectRequestState')) throw new Error('Run step 7 first.');
let payload; try { payload = JSON.parse(rpc.result.content[0].text) } catch (e) { payload = undefined }

request.description: GET /orders returns only this customer's orders: the approved chair is there, the rejected monitor is not.

exec: if (!pm.collectionVariables.get('approvedOrderId')) throw new Error('Run step 6 first.');
let payload; try { payload = JSON.parse(rpc.result.content[0].text) } catch (e) { payload = undefined }

pm.test('both placed orders are listed', () => { const ids = payload.orders.map(o => o.orderId); pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('smallOrderId')); pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('approvedOrderId')); });
pm.test('the rejected monitor was never ordered', () => pm.expect(payload.orders.map(o => o.productId)).to.not.include('p007'));

item.name: 10. order — DELETE is denied by gateway policy

request.description: The order API supports DELETE, but deny-all-delete blocks it before the backend is called.

exec: if (!pm.collectionVariables.get('approvedOrderId')) throw new Error('Run step 6 first.');
let payload; try { payload = JSON.parse(rpc.result.content[0].text) } catch (e) { payload = undefined }

request.description: A separate read proves the denied DELETE changed nothing.

exec: if (!pm.collectionVariables.get('approvedOrderId')) throw new Error('Run step 6 first.');
let payload; try { payload = JSON.parse(rpc.result.content[0].text) } catch (e) { payload = undefined }
